issues.location: "Remembering an answer instead of recomputing it" section: "`calls`, the total number of invocations including cache hits, grows linearly too, because each of those O(*n*) real computations only ever makes 3 recursive calls (one per coin) before returning."
issues.problem: Re-derived by hand from MinCoinsMemo's own `if (c <= amount)` guard for coins {1,4,5}: a computed node for amount 1, 2 or 3 can only recurse on coin 1 (coins 4 and 5 don't fit yet) -- 1 recursive call, not 3; amount 4 can recurse on coins 1 and 4 but not 5 -- 2 calls, not 3. Only computed nodes for amount >= 5 make all 3. Summing the actual per-node fan-out for amount=10 (1+1+1+2+3+3+3+3+3+3 = 23, plus the 1 initial invocation = 24) reproduces the article's own measured calls=24 exactly; assuming a uniform 3-per-node would predict 31, which the article's own table does not show. This is the kind of absolute claim (only/always/every) EDITORIAL_BRIEF.md's pilot-round lessons ask writers to scope. It does not change any printed number and the article's linear-growth conclusion still holds (the boundary effect is O(1), bounded by the largest coin), but the specific mechanistic sentence overclaims uniformity the code does not have.
issues.fixLooksLike: Scope the claim, e.g. "each of those O(n) real computations makes at most 3 recursive calls (one per coin that still fits) -- 3 for every amount at or above the largest coin's value, fewer only for the handful of amounts below it" -- or drop the specific fan-out number and point to the measured linear `calls` column as the evidence instead.
